title: Rav Acha bar Tachlifa
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was a student of Rava (Bava Kamma 34b; Sanhedrin 24a), for he raised an objection against Rava, and he spoke in Rava's name (Eruvin 68b).

While Rava was still alive, he sat with Ravina, as in Gittin 73a: someone came before Ravina, and when Ravina ruled, Rav Acha bar Tachlifa objected. The matter reached Rava, who ruled like Rav Acha bar Tachlifa. In Eruvin 40a, concerning the makers of wedding canopies: Ravina permitted them—Rava bar Tachlifa [which Hyman understands as an abbreviation of Rav Acha bar Tachlifa] said to Ravina—they went and asked Rava.

In Eruvin 63a it is related that Rabbi Elazar of Hagronya and Rav Acha Tachlifa visited Rav Acha son of Rav Ika, in the town of Rav Acha bar Yaakov. Rav Acha bar Tachlifa said, “Should we not show consideration for the elder?” Rabbi Elazar of Hagronya said, “Thus said Rav.” In Eruvin 100a, Rav Acha bar Tachlifa said to Abaye, “He who permitted it to you permitted it in accordance with Rabbah.” Hyman prefers the Dikdukei Soferim reading there, which has Rav Tachlifa speaking to Abaye.

notes.text: Rashi identifies the people in Eruvin40a as makers of wedding canopies. Hyman interprets Rava bar Tachlifa as an abbreviation of Rav Acha bar Tachlifa.

The named Eruvin63a text varies Abba/Acha between adjacent paragraphs and says “Thus said Rava,” while Hyman’s supplied text says Rav. Hyman’s preferred Rav Tachlifa reading in Eruvin100a is also preserved as his textual judgment.

The inspected Eruvin 40a directly reads Rava bar Tachlifa; Rashi explains the canopy makers. Hyman’s expansion to Rav Acha remains his proposal. Eruvin 63a has Abba in the arrival sentence and Acha in the following objection, and reads Rava where Hyman gives Rav. Eruvin 100a directly has Acha bar Tachlifa’s reply; the preferred Dikdukei Soferim reading was not independently inspected.
